responsibilities: Model company data in dbt on Redshift: layered, tested, documented models built to outlive you
Ship and run the company KPI dashboard in Lightdash, plus self-serve analytics for every team
Own metric modeling and propose the definitions the whole company runs on. Sign-off sits with data leadership, and you make every number defensible
Keep the ingestion layer running day to day (Fivetran connectors, existing ETL jobs), in close coordination with engineering
Act as a partner to our teams and turn ambiguous business questions from Finance, RevOps, Product, and CS into trusted, self-serve answers

Shape the data foundation before the function scales. As a Head of (Internal) Data & AI and a further Engineers join, you set the standards they inherit and go deeper on the architecture the whole company trusts.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Model company data in dbt on Redshift: layered, tested, documented models built to outlive you
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: quality language saturates the JD — 'layered, tested, documented', 'reliable, safe & scalable', 'rock-solid', 'You document, test, and monitor by default' — against one 'fast-growing startup' aside.
evidence.domain_risk: turn it into the single source of truth the whole company runs on, from ARR to product adoption
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate: the role owns internal company reporting ('from ARR to product adoption') for Finance and RevOps, with no regulatory, audit or patient-data responsibility named despite the care-sector product.
evidence.collaboration_width: Finance; RevOps; Product; Customer Success; engineering; data leadership
evidence.data_team_maturity: As our first dedicated analytics hire, you partner directly with Finance, RevOps, Product, and Customer Success
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Early: 'As our first dedicated analytics hire' and 'Shape the data foundation before the function scales' place this before the data function exists, even though the stack is already live.
evidence.jd_authorship: Keep the ingestion layer running day to day (Fivetran connectors, existing ETL jobs), in close coordination with engineering
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Hiring manager: the entire stack is named with its actual state — 'The modern stack (Redshift, dbt, Fivetran, Lightdash) is already live' — and sign-off boundaries are spelled out.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Act as a partner to our teams and turn ambiguous business questions from Finance, RevOps, Product, and CS into trusted, self-serve answers
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Mixed: Finance, RevOps, Product and Customer Success are named together twice as equal partners, with self-serve analytics for every team on top.
evidence.autonomy_level: As Senior Analytics Engineer, you own voize's company data from the warehouse to the dashboards.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic: the role owns the whole layer and sets what follows — 'you set the standards they inherit' — with only metric sign-off reserved to data leadership.
evidence.ai_role: ensuring the data voize and our AI layer runs on are reliable, safe & scalable
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_enabler: the role builds the data foundation voize's AI layer runs on, and separately expects AI-assisted working ('a track record of automating & building workflows with AI') — both signals present, so the enabler classification takes precedence.
evidence.testing_framing: You document, test, and monitor by default, and finishing the 10% that makes a model trustworthy
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility: testing and monitoring are stated as default behaviour the candidate owns, and the first responsibility bullet requires 'layered, tested, documented models'.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: turning their questions into numbers everyone trusts
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High: trust is the role's framing from the mission line onward — 'you make every number defensible', 'the architecture the whole company trusts' — with the fear being numbers the business cannot rely on.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: The modern stack (Redshift, dbt, Fivetran, Lightdash) is already live: you make it rock-solid
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Fix/scale: the JD states the stack 'is already live' and the job is to make it 'rock-solid', plus keeping existing Fivetran connectors and ETL jobs running.
evidence.work_arrangement: You decide when you work best, that means flexible working hours and a good hybrid set-up.
evidence.loss_aversion: Risk framing is the spine of the JD: 'ensuring the data voize and our AI layer runs on are reliable, safe & scalable' and 'you make every number defensible', with trust named as the output the business buys.
